headline: Recommended $1,000 increase to retiree cost-of-living maximum, plus acceptance of $24,476 traffic grant and $14,000 cultural grant.
summary: Stone Consulting presented the city's retiree health benefit (OPEB) valuation, which put the unfunded liability at $137 million. Auditor Kenny Costa said a formal policy on OPEB funding after 2034 would be ideal, since the city now pays these costs as they come due from the General Fund. The total deficit fell $127,000 after the Council on Aging received a formula grant.
decisions: Recommended that the City Council accept the FY27 MRST/Traffic Court grant of $24,476, 3-0.
Recommended that the City Council accept the $14,000 Mass Cultural Council grant, 3-0.
Recommended that the City Council approve a $1,000 increase to the cost-of-living adjustment maximum base for retirees, from $14,000 to $15,000, 3-0.

# Budget & Finance Standing Committee

Thursday, November 5, 2026 – 5:30 p.m.
Harbormaster’s Conference Room
19 Harbor Loop
Gloucester, MA 01930
and via Zoom
-Minutes-

**Present:** Chair Councilor Scott Memhard; Vice Chair Councilor Tony Gross; Councilor Patti-Ann Page

**Also Present:** Auditor, Kenny Costa (remote); Interim Police Chief, Michael Gossom

Meeting called to order at 5:30 p.m.

*This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.*

*Agenda items were taken out of order and the minutes reflect these changes.*

Councilor Memhard announced the names of the B&F Committee members in attendance and City staff who were in attendance in person and on Zoom.

## 1. Memorandum from the Interim Police Chief requesting acceptance of the FY27 MRST/Traffic Court grant in the amount of $24,476

**Summary of Discussion:** Interim Police Chief, Michael Gossom stated that this was an annual grant that the City had been receiving since 2019. He stated that it helped fund traffic enforcement.

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a federal grant from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and passed through the Mass. Executive Office of Public Safety and Security’s Office of Grants and Research (OGR), FF Y27 Municipal Road Safety Grant Program in the amount of $24,476 for the purpose of traffic safety. There is no local matching requirement for the grant and the period is from November 1, 2026 through September 15, 2027.

## 2. Memorandum from the City Auditor requesting review and discussion of the City’s FY2026 OPEB Actuarial Valuation Reports (cont. from October 22, 2026)

**Summary of Discussion:** Auditor, Kenny Costa stated that the Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) report was presented to the City every two years. He stated that OPEB was a large liability that the City needed to fund, and there was a plan to fund it more meaningfully once the retirement liability was fully funded in 2034.

Joan Moreau, Stone Consulting shared her screen.

Joan Moreau stated the above.

[Slide 1 – City of Gloucester, Other Post-Employment Benefits, July 1, 2025 Actuarial Valuation, Results Meeting, November 5, 2026. Presenters: Joan Moreau, ASA, FCA, MAAA; Kevin Gabriel, FSA, MAAA. Stone Consulting, Inc., 5 West Mill Street, Suite 4, Medfield MA 02052, T. (508) 359-9600 F. (508) 359-0190, e-mail: JMoreau@stoneconsult.com]

**Overview – Key Funding Results 7/1/25**

- Trust Assets: $3.0M (+59% from 2023)
- Plan Liabilities: $139.8M (+16% from 2023)
- Funded Pct: 2.2% (+37% from 2023)
- Unfunded Liability: $137M

**Annual Funding**

- City Cash Contribution FY26: $200,643
- Plus PAYGO (Retiree Claims): $7.5M
- Actuarially Determined Contribution (ADC): $10.6M

**Key Assumptions:** Discount rate: 6.75%; Ultimate Medical Trend: 5.0% (was 4.5%); Long-term Inflation: 2.5%

Joan Moreau stated the above.

[Slide 3 – Funding Progress. Chart: Funded Status. 7/1/2023: 1.58%; 7/1/2024: 2.03%; 7/1/2025: 2.16%; 7/1/2026: 2.50%. Pay-as-you-go funding + $200k from free cash]

[Slide 4 – Actuarially Determined Contribution FY2026. Chart: ADC – Amortization $7.5, Normal Cost $3.1; Actual Funding – PAYGO $7.5, Cash $0.2. 30-year amortization of unfunded liabilities; 3% annual increase]

Kevin Gabriel, Stone Consulting stated the above.

[Slide 5 – Changes in Liability July 2023 to July 2025. Two-Year Changes in Total OPEB Liability: July 1, 2023 $120.2M; Interest (2 years) 16.3; Normal Cost (2 years) 5.9; Claim/Trends 6.2; Population changes 4.1; Benefit payments (12.9); July 1, 2025 $139.8M]

[Slide 6 – Claims & Trends: Massachusetts GIC experience. MA Per-Capita Spending (2024): $11,663, +5.7% Year-over-year. US Total Health Expenditures (2024): $5.3T, +7.2% Year-over-year. Health Share % of US Economy: 18.0%, Up from 17.7% in 2023.

The FY26 Crisis:
- GIC covers ~460,000 state employees, retirees & dependents
- March 2025—Deficit threatened to exhaust claim funds by May
- Apr 2025—Gov. Healey filed supplemental budget
- $240M for GIC passed by Legislature
- FY2026 still began with a $77M deficiency

Cost Drivers:
- Hospital & provider costs
- Pharmacy spend +$1.5B (2024); GLP-1 weight-loss drugs a major factor

GIC Response FY27:
- FY2027 premiums up 7.5% across all plans
  - Non-Medicare +8%
  - Medicare: +4% – 7.5%
- No increase to copays/deductibles
- Removed coverage for certain GLP-1 weight-loss drugs]

Joan Moreau stated the above.

[Slide 7 – Historical Trends. Average Monthly Premiums, 2022–2026. Individual Commercial Plans: 9.4% average annual increases; Family Commercial Plans: 8.1% average annual increases; Medicare Plans: 5.3% average annual increases]

[Slide 8 – Population: Participation Rates. Changes in enrollment patterns.

| Coverage | Current | Prior | Actual Retirees |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Participation | 75.0% Current (2025) | 75.0% Prior (2023) | 86% |
| Spouse Coverage (Pre-65) | 25.0% | 25.0% | 49% |
| Spouse Coverage (Post-65) | 50.0% | 50.0% | 61% |
| Family Coverage Rate (Pre-65) | 25.0% | 25.0% | 49% (39 out of 79 pre-65 retirees) |

Additional Participation Rates: 70.0% Life Insurance; 85% Pre-86 Medicare Eligibility; 100% Current Retirees

Optimistic assumptions: Participation rates reflect current active elections. In our opinion, the current retiree population is a better indicator of future participation rates. Cost to change participant rate assumptions: $20M (14% increase)]

Kevin Gabriel stated the above.

[Slide 9 – Population: Demographic Shifts. Key population and plan selection changes.

Plan Selection Trend: Commercial HMO Plans. Retirees are electing managed care HMO plans over indemnity plans. GIC response to GLP-1 utilization 7/1/25.

Active Population: Unknown increase (method change). 905 Current; unknown increase. N/A Prior.

Plan Maturity Assessment: Ratio of Active to Retiree Liabilities: 0.54x (Active Liabilities to Retiree Liabilities Ratio).

Plan Status: Mature. A ratio below 1.0 signals that the pension plan is in a more mature, “pay-out” phase rather than an “accumulation” phase. → Retiree premium payments may be large as a % of payroll, straining current budgets.]

[Slide 10 – Results: Financial statement information (in millions)

| (in millions) | 7/1/2025 6.75% (fund) (current valuation) | 6/30/2026 4.77% (GASB) (current valuation) | 6/30/2025 5.20% (GASB) (prior valuation) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total OPEB Liability (Active 49.3; Inactive 90.5) | $139.8 | $181.2 | $152.2 |
| Assets (Market Value) | $3.0 | $3.6 | $3.0 |
| Net OPEB Liability (Unfunded) | $136.8 | $177.6 | $149.2 |
| Normal Cost / Svc Cost | $2.98 | $4.98 | $4.29 |
| Pay-As-You-Go (Premiums + Implicit Subsidy) | $7.52 | $7.52 | $6.15 |]

## GASB Discount Rate Calculation

Slide 11

- → liabilities are discounted using the long-term expected rate of return (6.75%) *prior to the depletion point*
- → liabilities are discounted using the municipal bond rate (4.67%) *after the depletion point*
- → an equivalent discount rate is calculated for all years

Chart title: GASB methodology projects Trust will fund benefits until 2035

Chart labels: Expected benefit payments current members; Contributions applied to current members; Assets; Asset Depletion; Long-term ROR on Assets; Bond Rate (4.67% at 6/30/26)

- Assumes $200k per year cash plus PAYGO
- Contributions (including PAYGO) cover new entrants before benefit payments for current members
- 6.75% long-term expected rate of return

## Asset Allocation

Slide 12

### None available

- Target asset allocation
  - Long-term expected rate of return
  - Used for funding
  - Used for funded portion of GASB depletion calculation and affects the blended rate

Asset allocation should align with the trust investment policy statement and risk tolerance, considering the expected timing of benefit payments and contribution schedule.

## Future Considerations

Slide 13

1. Lower your balance sheet liability: Consider **a formal commitment to fund OPEB** with *a % of the decrease* in pension appropriations after pension is funded.

For example, either funding plan a. or funding plan b. shown below would remove the GASB depletion point as of 6/30/2026.

   a. Flat $5M beginning in FY2036
   b. An initial amount of $3.5M in FY2036, increasing by 3% / year

2. Adopt more conservative assumptions to avoid future losses:
   - Change expected participation and spouse/family plan assumptions to reflect actual experience – **liability increase**
   - Possible mitigation: increase to 7.0% long-term expected rate of return *if merited* by the asset allocation and current capital market assumptions – **liability decrease**

**Joan Moreau** stated the above.

**Kenny Costa** stated that adopting a formal policy on OPEB contributions after 2034, as had been suggested, would be ideal. He noted that the City was currently funding OPEB in a Pay as You Go manner, which was paid out of the General Fund.

### 3. Memorandum from the Arts, Culture and Events Coordinator requesting acceptance of the Mass Cultural Council Grant in the amount of $14,000 (cont. from October 22, 2026)

**Summary of Discussion:** None.

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a Massachusetts State FY27 Local Cultural Council Grant from the Mass. Cultural Council in the amount of $14,000 for the purpose of supporting cultural life in the City. There is no local matching requirements for the state grant and the grant period is from October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

### 4. Memorandum from the Executive Director of the Gloucester Contributory Retirement System Board regarding a cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) increase.

**Summary of Discussion:** Auditor, Kenny Costa stated that that this would increase the amount each retiree received by $30 beginning on July 1, 2027.

There was a brief discussion regarding the future funding of the retirement system.

There was a brief discussion regarding the other units in the retirement system, which included the City, CATA, and the Housing Authority.

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council approve an increase of $1,000 to the cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) maximum base pursuant to the provisions of Chapter 32, Section 103 (j) inserted by Section 19 of Chapter 188 of the Acts of 2010, from a COLA maximum base of $14,000 to $15,000.

### 5. Memorandum from the City Auditor regarding accounts having expenditures which exceed their authorization & Auditor’s Report and other related business

**Summary of Discussion:** Auditor, Kenny Costa stated that the total deficit had decreased $127,000 due to the Council on Aging receiving the formula grant.

**No motion offered.**

**MOTION:** On a motion by Councilor Gross, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to adjourn at 6:24 p.m.

**Submitted by:** Lynds Jones, Legislative Aide.

**Documents submitted at the meeting:** Presentation by Stone Consulting.

**Matters appearing on the agenda that are to be continued:** None.

**Meeting Recording:** https://www.gloucester-ma.gov/1097/Past-Remote-Public-Meetings
